_schema.applies_to: matcher on {models, periods, results}; null = any. models: endogenous_pension_exogenous_labour (Table 2), endogenous_labour_no_pension (Table 3); periods: claim periods (financial-year end years); results: certified
_schema.status: the comparison status this annotation sets, where it sets one; at most one status-setting annotation matches a result
_schema.basis: traceability: raw/pages_layout.txt (PDF page), engine files at the certified pin, or the measured artifact results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json

annotations.text: CBP's figures are net fiscal impacts after a behavioural response: parents choose pension contributions with labour income fixed (Table 2), or choose labour supply with no pension (Table 3), and bunch at £100,000 when that leaves them at least £1,000 better off. PolicyEngine's counterpart is a static cost with no behavioural response, so the two measure different things. CBP publishes no static leg.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 8 (section 1.3.7, Table 2 and note), PDF page 10 (section 1.4.6, Table 3 and note); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json behavioural_response 'none (static)'

annotations.text: CBP's subsidy includes Tax-Free Childcare: its tables assume £500 of Tax-Free Childcare per child (the model description says up to £2,000). The PolicyEngine counterpart therefore removes both £100,000 limits and adds Tax-Free Childcare to the three free-hours entitlements.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 5 (section 1.2.3: 'Up to £2000 is then added to the subsidy to simulate the effect of Tax Free Childcare') and PDF pages 8 and 10 (table notes: '£500 utilisation of TFC'); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json worlds.free_hours_and_tfc

annotations.text: CBP assumes every eligible family uses the full working-parent hours, and gives every child two parents and no siblings. PolicyEngine uses the data's own take-up and hours-usage draws and its household composition.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 5 (section 1.2.2: 'every child has two parents and no siblings') and PDF pages 8 and 10 (table notes: 'full utilisation of FCWP')

annotations.text: CBP's population is synthetic: children from ONS births for England, each given two parents whose incomes are drawn from the 2022-23 Survey of Personal Incomes (ages 25 to 44). CenTax's Appendix D says the two estimates differ principally because CenTax observes in administrative data what the synthetic model had to assume, and names the treatment of frictions as the most consequential assumption.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 4-5 (sections 1.2.1-1.2.2); sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 100-101 (printed pages 99-100, Appendix D)

annotations.text: The appendix gives no sign rule for its tables, and its values are carried as printed. CenTax reads them as revenue raised. PolicyEngine's value is negative for a cost to the Exchequer.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 8 and 10 (titles and notes state no sign rule); sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 100 (printed page 99: 'CBP estimate that abolishing the threshold would raise between £130 million and £425 million in 2030')

annotations.text: CenTax quotes this cell as £425 million for 2030; the appendix prints 0.427 (£427 million) for 2029/30.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 10 (Table 3, Abolish Cliff, 2029/30); sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 100 (printed page 99, Appendix D)

annotations.text: CBP's columns are financial years (2026/27 is 2026-27). PolicyEngine's annual period 2026 runs the 2026-27 rules: policyengine-uk sets each government parameter for year Y to its value on 30 April of Y.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 8 and 10 (column labels); policyengine_uk 2.89.2 utils/parameters.py convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters, called in tax_benefit_system.py process_parameters
